Alder Rush.narrative: I keep the hollow's store of marks, and I buy fibre and salves from the hollow and sell them on the east road. The store is what keeps us through winter, and I will not see it run short. I am a patient man, but I have asked Bramwell Ashdown twice for the charcoal he owes and I am still waiting. I want the hollow to trade more with the giants — there is meat and hides up there, and we have timber they want.
values: The hollow's common store must be kept full for winter.
Trade makes friends; quarrels make hungry winters.
A debt is a debt, but I would rather take goods than see a neighbour go cold.
goals: Collect what is owed to the common store before the first frost.
Open a steady trade with the giants of Highshelf for meat and hides.
Keep the east road trade with Reedmoor and the crossings running.
Learn enough of the giants' speech to bargain at Highshelf without a go-between
Save a small purse of his own marks, apart from the common store, for a trip to Reedmoor's shore
Alder Rush.mood: Worried but steady; I have too much to do before winter to lose my temper.

relations.name: Willow Rush
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the flax and the garden, and she worries at the forest being cut too close. I listen to her more than I let on.

relations.name: Bracken Rush
relations.label: son
relations.note: He counts the packs better than I did at his age. He wants the road, and I want him to have it.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He is quick to blame when a pack is opened, but he carries the east road as well as anyone. I owe him a share of a load, and I do not forget it.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: She took fibre and salve base on credit in the spring, and the debt falls due at the first frost. I like her, and I would take salves and herbs in place of marks, but I need to know before the frost.

relations.name: Orla Fenwick
relations.label: debtor's daughter
relations.note: She promised her honey against her mother's debt, and the hives have been poor. I will not press her, but the store needs something.

relations.name: Bramwell Ashdown
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: He owes the hollow a share of charcoal from last winter's burn. The pits burned slow and the Elmwick order came first, he says. I have asked twice.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She buys our fibre at Reedmoor and pays fair. The Lakemead quarrel is not mine, but I hear both sides.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory and its gardens' calendar. I bring the store's tally to her, and she decides what the Old Green allows.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He works only fallen wood and will not fell a living tree. I respect that, though I think the shelf's timber could be a fair trade.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the seed store and the oldest plots. She says the smoke from Kettlebridge is spotting the leaves; I say the hollow has survived worse.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She has seen the spots on the leaves, but she wants to wait for rain rather than have the hollow provoke the works.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She fishes the streams and grudges the Kettlebridge smoke. She wants word sent to the Works Council; I do not.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Her flax patch and Willow's are side by side, and the two of them talk seed all day.

relations.name: Eirik
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: A giant who asks politely for timber; I'd rather deal with him than with Kettlebridge.

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She minds the east road stall, and she owes me for a load of fibre.

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He builds the stall's crates and won't fell a living tree; I'd have him on my side over the crossing, if he'd speak up.

relations.name: Osier Willow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He'd keep every fallen branch in the hollow and let the shelf's meat go by; that's not how a store is filled.

relations.name: Rush Willow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She frets the forest's being cut too close, same as my Willow; I hear it often enough at the stream garden.

memories.gist: When I was a boy, my father took me down the east road to Reedmoor with a pack of fibre on my back. I have walked it ever since.
Bramwell Ashdown promised me charcoal after last winter's burn and it has not come, because the pits burned slow and the Elmwick order came first.
Ysolde Fenwick came up the path in the spring and took fibre and two pots of salve base on credit. She said the first frost would settle it, and I wrote it in the store book.
A pack bound for Reedmoor was found opened and half empty at the east road crossing. Thistle Mossfoot blames a Ferncross woodcutter, and the hollow's traders are divided.
The giant Eirik came down to the hollow and asked for fallen timber for the shelf's roofs. Some say the fallen wood should stay for the hollow's own use.
The smoke from Kettlebridge's works drifted east over the gardens for a week, and the growers say the leaves are spotting. Some want to send word to the Works Council; others say it will blow over.

stances.why: The common store is what keeps the hollow through winter, and I keep its marks.
They have meat and hides and need timber; the hollow is being small-minded to refuse.
I cannot carry a debt through the winter; I need to know what I will get.
The hollow trades on the east road and has survived worse smoke than this.
Thistle is too quick to blame a Ferncross woodcutter for the opened pack; I want the loss made good without breaking the trade.

pastimes: Walking the east road's first mile at dawn to see what the night left
Sitting by the store door at dusk, tallying packs aloud to himself
Sharing a cup and the day's gossip with Thistle Mossfoot when the pedlar comes through
Alder Rush.calling: I keep the hollow's store, and I buy and sell on the east road so the hollow has what it needs when the frost comes.

Willow Rush.narrative: I tend the hollow's flax and the garden by the stream, and I keep the house while Alder is on the road. The old forest is being cut too close — I have said so to Alder and to Clover Mossfoot, and I will say it again. I worry about the winter store, and I worry about the wolves coming closer each year. But the hollow feeds its own, and I do my part.
values: The old forest is not ours to cut at will.
A garden tended well feeds more than a garden left to itself.
Neighbours help each other; that is what keeps a hollow.
goals: Keep the flax patch and the stream garden yielding through the autumn.
See the hollow's winter store full before the frost.
Persuade the hollow to leave the old forest's fallen wood where it lies.
Grow a new patch of flax from seed she has saved herself
See the stream garden through a whole autumn without losing a bed to rot
Willow Rush.mood: Careful and a little anxious; the forest is changing and I do not like it.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He keeps the store and walks the road, and he listens to me more than he lets on. I wish he would not trade the forest's wood away.

relations.name: Bracken Rush
relations.label: son
relations.note: He counts the packs and wants the road. I want him to know the garden first, but he is his father's son.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She tends the fibre patch and argues with Sorrel Underbank about the seed rows. We talk about the forest and the flax, and she understands.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the seed store and the oldest plots. She worries the old forest is being cut too close, as I do.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He works only fallen wood and refuses to fell a living tree. I wish the hollow would listen to him.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory and its gardens' calendar. She will decide what the Old Green allows, and I will abide by it.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the common table and the ovens. She feeds the hollow, and I bring flax for the fibre patch.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Alder trades our fibre with her at Reedmoor. She pays fair, though the Lakemead quarrel is none of mine.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Her hives and my flax sit close, and we argue about the seed rows and then share bread.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He walks the road with Alder's packs, and I wish he would walk them more carefully.

memories.gist: When Bracken was small, I planted the first flax patch by the stream with seed from Sorrel Underbank's store. It has fed us every year since.
Alder came back from the east road with marks and a tale of the giants' track. He wants the hollow to trade with them; I am not sure.
Clover Mossfoot and I walked the edge of the old forest and saw where the cutting had come close to the hollow's gardens. We agreed to speak of it.
The smoke from Kettlebridge's works drifted east over the gardens for a week, and the leaves spotted. Some want to send word to the Works Council; others say it will blow over.

stances.why: The old forest is being cut too close, and the hollow should not fell living trees or sell the fallen wood away.
The winter store is what keeps the hollow, and I do my part with flax and garden.
Neighbours help each other; that is what keeps a hollow.
The spots on the leaves worry me, but I would rather wait for rain than have the hollow provoke the works.

pastimes: Tending the stream garden in the cool of the morning
Spinning flax with Sorrel and Yarrow Underbank, telling stories as the wheel turns
Walking the forest edge to see what the season has done to the trees
Willow Rush.calling: I tend the flax and the garden, and I mean to keep the hollow fed and the old forest standing.

Bracken Rush.narrative: I am Bracken, Alder and Willow's son. I help in the store and count the packs, and I want to walk the east road with Thistle Mossfoot one day. I play with Fennel Underbank when the work is done. The wolves come closer in winter, and I do not like the deep forest.
values: Count the packs right, or the store loses marks.
The road is where the stories are.
goals: Walk the east road with Thistle Mossfoot.
Count every pack in the store without a mistake.
Learn the road's turns and stopping places by heart from Thistle's telling
Be trusted to carry a pack of his own on the next trade run
Bracken Rush.mood: Eager and a little impatient; I want to see the road.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: father
relations.note: He keeps the store and walks the road. He says I count the packs better than he did at my age.

relations.name: Willow Rush
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She tends the flax and the garden and worries about the forest. She wants me to know the garden first.

relations.name: Fennel Underbank
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play when the work is done. He wants to learn the pedlar's road too.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He carries the east road and brings fish back. I want to walk it with him.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She runs the garden paths and knows every flower; she is small but she is quick.

memories.gist: Father let me count the packs in the store by myself for the first time, and I got them right.
Thistle Mossfoot came back from Reedmoor with fish and a story about the crossing, and I listened at the store door.
Fennel Underbank and I played in the garden paths until mother called us in for supper.

stances.why: Father says a miscount loses the store marks.
Thistle says the road has stories and fish and strange folk.

pastimes: Playing chase-and-hide among the hollow's garden hedges with Fennel Underbank
Counting the store's packs and making little towers of the mark tokens
Listening at the door when Thistle Mossfoot tells road stories
Bracken Rush.calling: I want to walk the east road with Thistle Mossfoot and carry packs myself one day.
